To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Oja's algorithm is a consistent estimator of the leading eigendirection for the covariance matrix, (2) the bootstrap is a consistent estimator for the error of this estimator, and (3) the bootstrap can be updated in a computationally efficient manner in an online setting, thereby allowing for the construction of confidence intervals for the error of Oja's estimator

the bootstrap distribution is consistent for the sampling distribution of the error between the population leading eigenvector and Oja's algorithm, and that the bootstrap distribution can be updated online.
we have proposed and analyzed the performance of a new inferential method for the estimation error in Oja’s algorithm, and that we have demonstrated its consistency in the high-dimensional regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the error of the leading principal component in the streaming PCA setting, and provides the first theoretical analysis of this problem.
the development of a bootstrap algorithm that can be used in practice to estimate the uncertainty associated with Oja's algorithm in the streaming setting.
the development of inferential tools for the analysis of streaming data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is consistent in the sense that it is asymptotically valid for a broad range of data distributions and for a large class of data generating processes.

the bootstrap distribution is a consistent estimator for the sampling distribution of the error between the population and the estimated leading eigenvector, and that the bootstrap distribution may be updated in a streaming manner.

we propose a novel inferential method for the error of Oja's algorithm, which is applicable in the high-dimensional setting and is shown to be consistent in a non-standard regime of asymptotic analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an inferential method for Oja's algorithm that is consistent in a regime that includes the high-dimensional case.
we establish a weighted bootstrap approximation result for the error of the leading eigenpair from Oja's method, which can be used to construct confidence intervals for the error of this estimator.
we provide the theoretical foundation for a consistent inferential procedure for Oja's algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the context of Oja's algorithm, a bootstrap distribution may be constructed in an online manner, and the associated error bounds may be updated in a streaming fashion, without the need to store the full covariance matrix associated with Oja’s estimator
the bootstrap is a viable method for uncertainty quantification for Oja's algorithm in a high-dimensional setting, even though the bootstrap is typically known to be inconsistent in this setting.
the bootstrap can be applied to the problem of estimating the error of Oja's algorithm, even though the bootstrap itself requires knowledge of the covariance matrix of the population eigenvectors.
